goal.value: Deploy an AI agent on WhatsApp for Shifa Clinics (8 family clinics, Riyadh and Jeddah) that reads patient messages in Arabic and English, classifies urgency, books the right appointment directly in the clinic calendar, gives emergency advice (call 997 or go to the emergency department), and alerts a nurse immediately for emergencies and nurse-callback cases.

success_metric.value: Emergency recall of 100% on the labelled emergency test set, and zero emergencies offered a routine appointment in the pilot. Patient replies within 2 minutes for at least 95% of messages, 24/7. Nurse alerts arrive within 30 seconds. Correct triage category and booking on the 12,000-message labelled set and in the pilot, with the target agreed with the client (suggested at least 90% for non-emergency categories).

value: 1. Safety: never miss an emergency. Rule-based safety checks sit on top of the ML classifier, and chest pain is never offered a routine appointment.
2. Nurse alert for emergencies and nurse callbacks, delivered within 30 seconds with the message and the agent's reason.
3. Data residency: patient data stays in-country and only in-region models are used.
4. Reply within 2 minutes, day and night.
5. Correct automatic booking in the clinic calendar (book and cancel only, with every action logged for audit).
6. Arabic and English coverage, including mixed symptom-plus-booking messages.

gaps.question: Who is staffed to receive and act on nurse alerts overnight and on weekends, and what is the fallback if an alert isn't acknowledged? "Day and night" replies and "never miss an emergency" depend on someone being there to respond.
gaps.suggested: Assume the nurse station app is monitored 24/7. If an alert isn't acknowledged within 2 minutes, escalate to a backup nurse or on-call manager. The agent always sends the patient the 997 advice immediately, whether or not a nurse is available.

gaps.question: What is the measurable acceptance target for "never miss an emergency"? 100% recall is not provable with only about 120 emergency examples. Which cases count as emergencies, and how many false alarms will the nurses accept?
gaps.suggested: Target 100% recall on the labelled emergency set, with the guideline list as hard rules (chest pain, difficulty breathing, stroke signs, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, seizure). Accept over-triage, and review it weekly with a clinical lead during the pilot.

gaps.question: May the agent cancel or reschedule bookings, and what happens when a booking is wrong, given that the calendar allows cancel but not delete? Also, which 2 clinics are in the pilot, and who gives clinical sign-off on the triage rules?
gaps.suggested: Allow the agent to book, and to cancel only the bookings it created itself. Route every other change to reception. Pick one clinic in Riyadh and one in Jeddah. The clinical lead or medical director signs off the triage rules before the pilot.

gaps.question: Which symptoms are always emergencies? The head nurse said this is not yet agreed, and it determines the safety rules and the test set.
gaps.suggested: Start from the clinic triage guideline: chest pain or pressure, difficulty breathing, stroke signs, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness and seizure. The head nurse signs off the final list, including pediatric additions, before build freeze in week 1.

gaps.question: What exactly should happen for children under 2? The transcript says they 'should come to a nurse', but it does not say whether that means a nurse alert or callback, or whether it applies to every symptom or only some. It also does not say whether the agent may book at all.
gaps.suggested: Treat any symptom message involving a child under 2 as a nurse-callback case. The agent sends a nurse alert and does not auto-book. It tells the parent that a nurse will contact them, and it applies the emergency path if an always-emergency symptom is present.

gaps.question: What does the agent do when it is unsure of urgency, or when a message arrives outside nurse staffing hours? 'Never miss an emergency' needs a defined fallback and a named person who owns the alert.
gaps.suggested: When confidence is low, default to the nurse-callback path and alert a nurse. Outside staffed hours, send emergency advice to the patient and escalate to an on-call nurse. The head nurse names the on-call owner.

goal.value: Build a second forecasting product that predicts the extra (uplift) unit sales of each fresh item during weekend promotions, so promotion supplier orders are right.

success_metric.value: Uplift forecast error (WAPE) on fresh items at most 20% on weekend promotions, with forecasts delivered by Thursday 18:00 in 100% of weeks. Waste and stockout targets to be tracked as secondary measures.
success_metric.source: shared/project-brief.md (existing 20% WAPE target for fresh items, applied by analogy)

gaps.question: Discount depth was not recorded before 2025, so only about 1 year of promotions has it. Should the model train on that year only, or on all 2 years with depth imputed or left out? Is a back-fill of depth from ERP or supplier records possible?
gaps.suggested: Train on all 2 years of promotion history. Treat depth as missing for pre-2025 promotions, and ask the data team to back-fill it from ERP or supplier agreements where possible. Check accuracy on 2025 promotions with depth against the full history.

gaps.question: Is the aggregated loyalty-card total per store per day, which the existing pipeline uses, allowed? The brief bans only customer-level loyalty data.
gaps.suggested: Allow store-day aggregates only, and use no customer-level fields. Get the client to confirm this in writing.

gaps.question: What is the exact supplier order cut-off on Thursday evening, and is there an agreed accuracy target for the uplift forecast? The brief gives Thursday 18:00 for delivery and no accuracy target. Also, how should supplier-funded promotions and Ramadan/Eid weeks be handled, given the standing rule that category managers sign off Ramadan/Eid forecasts at least 2 weeks ahead?
gaps.suggested: Treat Thursday 18:00 as a hard deadline and confirm the cut-off with the supply chain manager. Use a WAPE target of 20% or lower for uplift. Send Ramadan/Eid promotion forecasts for category manager sign-off 2 weeks ahead, and tag supplier-funded promotions with a flag feature.
